key_insight: Sampling one cell twice (its data, then a written '1') through one comparator cancels amplifier offset and Cs/Cbl spread: a reference-free, single-ended read suited to TFT periphery over 3D arrays.
killer_doubt: Destructive 1T1C read needs one amp per bitline (~0.2-0.3 um2 at 1b pitch); a 180 nm amp is ~50x larger. Read grows to ~3x tRC (~135 ns), ~3x array energy.
decisive_experiment: IGZO TFT test chip (university fab, ~$250k): 64 1T1C cells per bitline with a self-referenced auto-zeroed comparator; measure residual offset, read BER versus Cs (1-5 fF), and total read latency at 85 C.
prior_art: Offset-cancelling bitline sense amps in recent production DRAM nodes; destructive self-reference reads in MRAM and FeRAM since the early 2000s.

key_insight: Append-only KV-cache mats touch rows in order, so a shift-register token can replace row predecode and be drawn at relaxed DUV pitch.
killer_doubt: Pitch-matched sub-wordline drivers at VPP ~3 V, not predecoders, dominate row periphery; decoder logic is ~3-5% of die (est.), so cutting 60% saves ~2-3%.
decisive_experiment: Desk layout study (~$30k) of a 1b-class mat: row-decoder versus sub-wordline-driver area, then with a token chain; plus a paged-attention trace replay measuring the share of non-sequential row hits.
prior_art: Serial-access memories (video-RAM SAM ports, FIFO DRAMs); display gate-driver-on-array shift registers; imec block-addressable CCD buffer memory.

key_insight: One etch and one decoder set shared by N layers is the right answer to Optane's per-deck mask cost, if layers could be addressed independently.
killer_doubt: Series layers cascade: one snapback (~1 V drop) overdrives the rest, so they fire together. Eight windows need ~16-24 V ramps; per-layer writes cannot be isolated; OTS endurance ~1e8-1e11.
decisive_experiment: Two- and three-layer OTS series stacks on 100 nm crosspoints (university fab, ~$200k): test whether snapbacks resolve as separate current spikes, window overlap over 1,000 devices, and per-layer write selectivity.
prior_art: Intel/Micron 3D XPoint (two decks, per-deck masks); selector-only / self-selecting chalcogenide memory work at Micron and SK hynix.

key_insight: A threshold switch plus capacitor under a global AC sustain is a real transistor-free bistable latch, as AC plasma panels showed across ~6e6 subpixels.
killer_doubt: OTS leakage ~0.1 nA drains 1 fF in ~5 us: ~200 kHz sustain at ~16 fJ/firing is ~14 W/GB (DDR5 refresh ~12 mW/GB), ~6e13 firings per decade.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate 100 OTS-plus-1 fF MIM cells (university fab, ~$150k); measure the bistable sustain window versus Vth spread and drift, the minimum sustain frequency at 85 C, and firings to failure.
prior_art: AC plasma display wall-charge memory effect; T-RAM thyristor bistable memory (2000s); OTS crosspoint selector arrays (3D XPoint).

key_insight: Charge-conserving capacitance collapse gives DC-free, near-noiseless pre-latch voltage gain with no matched transistor in the path: a low-voltage complement to charge-transfer pre-sensing.
killer_doubt: Fixed sense-node parasitics (~1-2 fF) cap gain at ~2-3x unless varactors reach ~10 fF (~0.5 um2 each at 2 nm EOT), versus ~0.2-0.3 um2 for a whole 1b sense amp.
decisive_experiment: 28-65 nm MPW (~$250k): sense amps with 2-10 fF accumulation-mode varactor preamps on 35 fF dummy bitlines; measure net gain, input-referred offset sigma over 10k amps and added latency versus an offset-cancelling baseline.
prior_art: MOS-varactor discrete-time parametric amplifiers in ADC residue stages; DRAM charge-transfer pre-sensing (Phase B N-04). In DRAM sense amps: none found.

key_insight: Floating-diffusion readout gives ~0.3 mV per electron at ~0.5 fF, so ~500-1,000 e- packets suffice and per-tier decoders and staircases disappear.
killer_doubt: imec IGZO CCDs clock at ~4-6 MHz: a 64-tier shift takes ~10-16 us, ~100x the claimed 100 ns. Poly-Si grain-boundary dark charge (~100 fA) fills 1,000 e- in ~2 ms.
decisive_experiment: Fold into the I-01064 test chip: planar then 8-tier IGZO CCD with a floating-diffusion output; measure per-transfer CTE versus clock (4-200 MHz), conversion gain and 85 C dark charge. ~$300k.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024 planar; IMW 2026 vertical 3D, via search snippet); CIS vertical CCD registers; Phase B N-08; I-01064.

key_insight: Recirculation through one regenerating node turns refresh into shifting; with IGZO's >200 s hold, one circulation every few seconds costs almost nothing.
killer_doubt: 512 tiers x 4 phases is ~2,000 transfers per pass: CTE 0.9999 keeps 82%, imec's >98% keeps ~0. A ~25 um stack in 100 nm holes is AR ~250.
decisive_experiment: Add 2,000-transfer recirculating loops to a planar IGZO CCD test chip (~$300k, shared with I-01064): measure cumulative loss and trailing charge; continue only if per-transfer loss is below 5e-5 at >=10 MHz.
prior_art: imec IGZO 3D CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024, IMW 2026); 1970s Si CCD bulk memories; Phase B N-08; I-00601 (same 200+-tier variant).

key_insight: Regenerating each packet once per 64-128-tier pass relaxes CTE to ~0.999-0.9995; writes go through a semiconductor channel, and imec reports >1e10 cycles without wear.
killer_doubt: Capacity tier, not DRAM: at imec's ~4-6 MHz a 64-128-tier pass is ~10-30 us; DRAM tRC (~45 ns) would need GHz word-plane clocks against ~100+ ns plane RC.
decisive_experiment: Planar 3-phase IGZO CCD loop (32-64 stages) with a regenerating amp at the end (university fab, ~$300k): per-transfer CTE at 4-200 MHz, fat zero, 85 C dark charge, error rate after 1e6 recirculations.
prior_art: imec IGZO 3D CCD buffer memory for CXL type-3 (IEDM 2024, IMW 2026); 1970s CCD and delay-line memories; Phase B N-08; I-06518, I-01064.

key_insight: Zero detection at the sense-amp stripe is nearly free and saves pin energy and bandwidth on all-zero sectors, compression with no decompression latency.
killer_doubt: All-zero 64 B sectors are rare in dense BF16/INT4 weights and KV (est. <5%), and 2:4 sparsity leaves none. It needs a JEDEC protocol change for ~1-5% I/O energy.
decisive_experiment: Software trace study (~$30k): share of all-zero 32/64 B sectors in LLM weights, KV cache, activations and OS pages across real serving workloads. Stop if below 10% of traffic.
prior_art: Zero-content caches and zero-value compression (ISCA/ICS literature); DDR4/DDR5 data-bus inversion; ZeroPoint compression IP; OS zero-page deduplication.

key_insight: Deposition-defined stacking with one hole etch is the only proven route below $0.1/GB, and IGZO gain cells are transistor-written (imec >1e12 cycles), so endurance is not the wall.
killer_doubt: NAND strings are series; random-access 2T0C needs lateral transistor pairs per tier (the 3D DRAM blocker). Even 0.2% per-tier killer defects give 0.998^300 = ~55% block yield.
decisive_experiment: Desk model (~$50k) of $/GB versus tier count from NAND per-tier cost and published IGZO 2T0C footprints; then a 4-8-tier vertical-channel IGZO 2T0C stack at a partner line, measuring per-tier Vt spread and defects.
prior_art: NEO Semiconductor 3D X-DRAM (NAND-like process); IMECAS 4-tier 2T0C (VLSI 2026); Kioxia 8-layer horizontal IGZO (IEDM 2025); Phase B N-43.

key_insight: Memory entrants die in the bust, not the boom (Qimonda 2009, Elpida 2012). A tapered, technology-neutral price floor makes an entrant fab bankable, like a power-purchase agreement.
killer_doubt: 10 EB is ~1/3 of a year's world DRAM bits (~25-30 EB, est.), ~$30-50B. Industry lobbied in July 2026 against market interventions and favors incumbent long-term contracts.
decisive_experiment: Policy pilot (~$500k): term sheet (performance thresholds, 0.5-1 EB, taper, floor price); model entrant-fab IRR with and without it through a 2012-style bust; seek non-binding letters of intent from 3-5 hyperscalers.
prior_art: Gavi pneumococcal AMC ($1.5B); Frontier carbon-removal AMC ($925M); CHIPS grants (Micron ~$6.1B) are supply-side. No memory AMC found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Error tolerance can be traded for tier yield, but only by bit significance: protect sign and exponent, relax mantissa bits (Phase B N-65).
killer_doubt: At raw 1e-3, a 70B BF16 model takes ~7e7 exponent-MSB flips (a ~0.01 weight becomes ~1e36). Tier yield is set by line shorts killing whole mats, beyond any BER tolerance.
decisive_experiment: Software fault injection (~$50k): inject 1e-5 to 1e-3 random flips into LLM weights and KV, with and without exponent protection; measure accuracy; model block yield versus line-short density per tier.
prior_art: Flikker (ASPLOS 2011); EDEN approximate DRAM for DNNs (MICRO 2019); Phase B N-62 (ECC-paid capacitor) and N-65 (significance-split).
